## Appearance

Wilfred Mott is notable for having hands that feel perpetually cold and fish-like.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Farewell P23](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0023)_

## Personality

Wilfred Mott is a character who has been noted for appearing remarkably pompous. Driven by ambition, he intends to enter politics in order to serve as a member of Parliament.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Regent’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v3 ch.Relationships P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004)_

## History

In his youth, Wilfred Mott defended [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) Harcourt's honor by getting into a fight with [Elias Purdy MacKinnon](../character/elias-purdy-mackinnon.md) after Elias criticized Nell's recitations, and he previously declared to his mother that [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) was the cleverest female student in school. Having written local newspaper pieces in the past, he was infatuated with [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) when she was seventeen. Years later, Wilfred traveled by train and ferry alongside [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) as they journeyed to [Portmaris](../codex/places.md#portmaris). While attending college, he joined [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md), Hugh, [Honora Hollis](../character/honora-hollis.md), and [Cressida Lindsay](../character/cressy-lindsay.md) on a walk along [Linden Avenue](../codex/places.md#linden-avenue). During Nell's term at [Wexcombe](../codex/places.md#wexcombe-college), Wilfred made an unpleasant proposal to her, which she did not accept.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022), [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002), [v2 XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country P0](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0000), [v3 ch.Farewell P0](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0000), [v3 ch.Farewell P2](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0002), [v3 ch.Farewell P10](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0010), +10 more_

### [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/hugh-carrow--wilfred-mott.md)

Although Wilfred Mott and [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) initially competed for the favor of a young lady starting in Volume 2, their relationship evolved over time. By Volume 3, the two had established a bond as constant friends.
